text: The Patriots offense is in genuine crisis after a 35-6 demolition by the Jaguars, a loss so lopsided it's raised fundamental questions about whether the team is deploying Drake Maye correctly in the first place—especially concerning given that New England ranks dead last in the NFL at 9.7 offensive points per game and Maye himself coughed up two interceptions and a fumble on Sunday, leading him to call his own performance and the offense's showing "unacceptable" as he searches for answers. The film analysis suggests systematic breakdowns in coverage and execution rather than isolated missteps, while defensive bright spots like Marcus Jones's first interception of the season offer little solace when the offense is this thoroughly dysfunctional and the Jaguars' Lawrence was shredding New England for three touchdowns, vindicating Jacksonville's response-focused preparation for the week. With Mike Vrabel now at the helm, there's clearly work to be done—not just in scheme but in how the entire offensive infrastructure is functioning—because an 9.7 points-per-game average isn't an outlier problem; it's evidence of something fundamentally wrong that demands answers more urgent than Maye's weekly mea culpas.
